item.title: Xinhua Headlines: How Chinese innovation drives shared growth from Shenzhen to Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-15
* Shenzhen offers a snapshot of this vibrant high-tech trade story. Total R&D spending in the city grew at an average annual rate of 12.9 percent from 2020 to 2024, and R&D intensity reached 6.67 percent, the highest among Chinese cities. The Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou innovation cluster has also topped the Global Innovation Index rankings. * Cooperation between Shenzhen and its Asia-Pacific partners advances along a well-defined track, featuring manufacturing, research and talent development, and the practical application of technology, said Chen Jiaxi, vice president of the Shenzhen Reform and Opening Up Executive Leadership Academy. * "The Shenzhen meeting will send a clear signal: China's commitment to high-standard opening up, to sharing opportunities with the Asia-Pacific, and to multilateralism remains firm," said Chen, who is also a professor at Shenzhen University. SHENZHEN, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- From a battery anode materials plant built from scratch in Indonesia to a surgical robot in a Kuala Lumpur operating room and solar panels atop a century-old Thai university, companies from China's southern tech hub of Shenzhen have established a presence across the Asia-Pacific region. Next week, as Shenzhen in Guangdong Province hosts the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the innovative, collaborative approach that Shenzhen embodies will take center stage. The numbers are significant. China's goods trade with other APEC members reached 26.29 trillion yuan (about 3.9 trillion U.S. dollars) in 2025, or nearly 60 percent of its total foreign trade, according to the General Administration of Customs. High-tech goods are an increasingly strong link: China's exports of such products to other APEC members rose 8.1 percent to 4.63 trillion yuan in 2025. Shenzhen offers a snapshot of this vibrant high-tech trade story. Total R&D spending in the city grew at an average annual rate of 12.9 percent from 2020 to 2024, and R&D intensity reached 6.67 percent, the highest among Chinese cities. The Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou innovation cluster has also topped the Global Innovation Index rankings. Cooperation between Shenzhen and its Asia-Pacific partners advances along a well-defined track, featuring manufacturing, research and talent development, and the practical application of technology, said Chen Jiaxi, vice president of the Shenzhen Reform and Opening Up Executive Leadership Academy. "The Shenzhen meeting will send a clear signal: China's commitment to high-standard opening up, to sharing opportunities with the Asia-Pacific, and to multilateralism remains firm," said Chen, who is also a professor at Shenzhen University. BUILDING LOCALLY BTR New Material Group (BTR), a Shenzhen-based battery materials maker, opened an anode material plant in Indonesia's Kendal Industrial Park in August 2024 -- the first overseas anode production base built by a Chinese company in the sector, said He Xueqin, the group's chairman. Before this plant, Indonesia had no lithium-ion battery anode manufacturing industry at all, He said. Then-Indonesian president Joko Widodo attended the opening, saying it brought the country a step closer to building an electric-vehicle ecosystem, the Economic Daily reported at the time. Two years on, a second phase is in full operation, doubling annual capacity to 160,000 tonnes. The Indonesian subsidiary's revenue jumped 161 percent year on year to 1.71 billion yuan in the first half of 2026, supplying battery makers in Japan, the Republic of Korea, Europe and the United States. Before the plant, Indonesia had already built a cathode materials industry from its nickel resources, and BTR added the anode link. "By 2026, separator and electrolyte production has also landed in Indonesia, completing the four main battery materials and laying a solid foundation for the electric-vehicle ecosystem," He said. The deeper shift is what BTR calls "chain-style overseas expansion," with the company having urged its strategic suppliers to move with it, helping them with local research, assessment and site selection. Packaging and crucible suppliers have already set up operations in Indonesia. Shenzhen SED Industry Co., Ltd. (SED), a subsidiary of China Electronics Corporation, is exporting plant-building capability itself. For an optical module project in Thailand, its design team analyzed years of local climate data rather than copying domestic designs, adding safeguards against heat and humidity in everything from equipment selection to insulation and cleanroom airtightness. At an electronics plant in Thailand's 304 Industrial Park, SED applied digital technology across design, construction and operations. Construction clashes fell by more than 95 percent, accidents by over 80 percent, and the plant went from blueprint to completion in just 270 days. The company now has more than 500 staff and over 1,300 overseas supply chain partners across APEC economies including Thailand, Vietnam and Malaysia, SED said. RESEARCH AND TALENT New plants need people who can run, maintain and improve them. Shenzhen's ties with the region are therefore extending beyond production lines into laboratories and classrooms. As of March 2026, BGI Group, a Shenzhen-based life science and genomics organization, had jointly trained students with more than 80 universities at home and abroad, including Chulalongkorn University and Mahidol University in Thailand, the University of Indonesia and the University of Malaya. These programs involved 4,490 students in total, 2,503 of them at master's or doctoral level. Such training is tied to research. With Chulalongkorn University, BGI is working on population aging, gut microbiome studies and thalassemia. In Indonesia, BGI signed an agreement in September 2026 with the health ministry's center for biomedical and health genomics to support the Biomedical and Genome Science Initiative, the country's first national genome program, covering joint research, platform development and local training. BGI describes its approach as "using projects to build disciplines, industries and talent." Since 2018, BGI has run 13 national-level training programs for more than 360 mid- and senior-level biotech professionals from Belt and Road partner countries, almost 60 percent of them from APEC members, and several alumni have become senior public health officials at home, the company said. TECHNOLOGY ON THE GROUND The ultimate test of sci-tech cooperation is whether it can serve local needs and improve everyday life. In a Kuala Lumpur operating room, orthopaedic surgeon Rajiv Rampal guided a Shenzhen-developed robot through a hip replacement. The machine, developed by Shenzhen-based Yuanhua Robotics, Perception and AI Technologies Ltd. (Yuanhua Tech) and manufactured in Hong Kong, completed its first Malaysian operation in July and had performed 21 procedures by early September. Unlike many surgical robots that are tied to specific implant brands, the Shenzhen robot runs on an open platform: all 21 operations used international-brand implants familiar to local doctors. AI algorithms plan for different implant brands, achieving sub-millimeter placement without changing surgeons' routines. "Let the machine adapt to the doctor, not the doctor to the machine," a Yuanhua Tech official said. Shenzhen's rapid technological innovation, coupled with Hong Kong's international quality control standards, gives Malaysia access to cutting-edge medical technology, an official with the Malaysian Chinese-language daily Kwong Wah Yit Poh said. At century-old Mahidol University in Thailand, 41 campus buildings are topped with solar panels. Huawei describes the project as the Asia-Pacific's largest single-site commercial and industrial solar-plus-storage system. This project serves a national goal. Thailand announced at the COP26 climate summit in 2021 that it would achieve carbon neutrality by 2050, and has encouraged rooftop solar via incentives and tighter safety standards. The university chose Huawei's smart photovoltaic solution: 15 megawatts of solar capacity, 600 kilowatt-hours of storage and optimisers, which is expected to save around 2.3 million U.S. dollars a year and cut carbon emissions by 11,000 tonnes. The optimisers allow more panels across the 41 rooftops and lift power output by 10 percent, while the storage provides backup power. The campus is part of a wider footprint. By early 2025, Huawei's digital power business had served over 1,000 Thai enterprises and installed 6 gigawatts of solar inverters, helping generate more than 6 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity and cut carbon dioxide emissions by more than 5 million tonnes, said Yu Junxiang, an official with Huawei's arm in Thailand. Taken together, Chen said, these cases show how Shenzhen, an urban test case for Chinese modernization, can serve a region: openness breeds cooperation and innovation drives shared growth, offering Asia-Pacific economies a viable path to build consensus, narrow development gaps and achieve shared prosperity. (Video reporters: Hui Peipei and Li Jiale; video editors: Hui Peipei, Roger Lott, Li Qin and Li Jiale)■

item.title: Preparations for APEC Shenzhen meeting ready: officials
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
This photo taken on Nov. 14, 2026 shows a press briefing at the media center for the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Liang Xu) SHENZHEN, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- Preparations for the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, south China, are ready, local officials said at a press briefing on Saturday. The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18 and 19, Wang Xi, deputy head of the provincial preparatory leading group, told the briefing. Wang said organizers had incorporated green practices, traditional Chinese and local Lingnan culture, and digital technologies into venue preparations and services. During the meeting week, Guangdong will offer 218 visitor sites and 43 routes, including two representative ones in Shenzhen. Organizers have upgraded key venues and conducted comprehensive rehearsals, and have arranged reception, accommodation, catering, transport, medical care and interpretation, as well as measures for communications, weather, public security, public health and city operations, Wang said. Shenzhen Mayor Li Yun said all venues and facilities were ready. The city has strengthened transport, power, communications and hotel services while minimizing inconvenience to residents' daily lives. The city has also introduced measures to make travel and daily transactions easier for visiting delegates. Dedicated channels for meeting representatives will be available at nine sea, land, air and rail ports. More than 100,000 foreign-language signs have been standardized, and over 7,000 AI translation devices have been installed at key locations. Taxis will provide bilingual announcements. More than 3,000 ATMs support cash withdrawal for foreign bank cards, while over 1,600 bank branches offer currency exchange. Shenzhen's metro fare gates will accept contactless payments with overseas bank cards. The city has also expanded its departure tax-refund program to 3,160 stores, including more than 1,000 offering instant refunds. Data released at the briefing also showed that Shenzhen has become the first city in the Chinese mainland to record more than 5 trillion yuan (about 744.6 billion U.S. dollars) in foreign trade. Shenzhen Customs said the city's imports and exports totaled 5.25 trillion yuan in the first 10 months of this year, up 40.9 percent year on year. Exports rose 19.7 percent to 2.71 trillion yuan, while imports surged 73.7 percent to 2.54 trillion yuan. ■ This photo taken on Nov. 14, 2026 shows a press briefing at the media center for the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Liang Xu)

item.title: China-Arab cooperation deepening traditional bonds, exploring new horizons
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
NANJING, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- On the sidelines of the Fifth China-Arab States Political Parties Dialogue being held in the eastern Chinese city of Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, an orca-shaped marine robot is outshining other smart devices, such as quadruped robots, in capturing the attention of participants. With streamlined contours and a metallic sheen, the marine robot "Orca Max" developed by Seahi Robotics can operate across the full ocean depth range from 0 to 10,000 meters. When introducing this robot to visitors, Cao Ying, co-founder of the company, said the cooperation meeting offered the Suzhou-based company a valuable opportunity to explore Arab markets. Free from manual remote control, the marine robot can carry out autonomous operations in complex ocean currents, lightless deep-sea zones and areas with no communication coverage. Freddy Elbaiady, vice president of the Egyptian Social Democratic Party and member of Egypt's House of Representatives, stopped at the booth to secure more detailed information about this product. "Egypt boasts numerous ports with strong demand for maritime shipping and vessel maintenance," he said, while adding that the robot has enormous potential in Egypt for vessel cleaning, the construction, operation and maintenance of marine new energy facilities, port inspection, dredging and deep-sea applications. Cao said that the robot has been deployed at more than 70 major ports worldwide. Driven by the company's self-developed AI model, the robot can provide safe, efficient and sustainable general-purpose ocean robotics solutions for global ocean development. The two-day meeting, which opened on Friday, has gathered over 100 leaders of political parties and organizations as well as business, think tank and media representatives from 22 Arab countries. The 2026 dialogue has achieved two milestones: full representation of all 22 Arab countries, and the inaugural China-Arab Business Dialogue on the Belt and Road Initiative as a side event. During the event, entrepreneurs from more than 200 Chinese and Arab firms shared experience on Belt and Road cooperation as well as collaboration in trade, investment, science and technology. Saleh Al Khabti, president of Acwa China, told Xinhua that he was pleased to learn that his hometown, the port city of Jeddah in Saudi Arabia, now has a direct shipping route linking it with Suzhou. The direct container shipping route he referred to opened in October, linking Suzhou's Taicang Port with Jeddah and cutting transit time by two to three weeks. He said the new logistics channel will facilitate trade between China, Saudi Arabia and the broader Middle East. Al Khabti added that the company opened its Beijing office in 2009, and established headquarters in Shanghai in 2023. In 2024, it inaugurated a Global Innovation Center in Pudong District of Shanghai, to foster collaboration in renewable energy, energy storage, green hydrogen and water desalination. "As part of our strategy in China, we aim to invest up to 30 billion U.S. dollars in China by 2030. We also plan to increase our procurement of Chinese equipment by 15 billion dollars annually, and we view Jiangsu Province as a key pillar for tapping promising cooperation opportunities in this area," he said. This year marks the 70th anniversary of the beginning of diplomatic relations between China and Arab countries, as well as the 10th anniversary of the launch of the China-Arab States Political Parties Dialogue mechanism. Figures from the International Department of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee show that China has signed Belt and Road cooperation documents with all 22 Arab countries, carrying out more than 200 cooperation projects that benefit nearly 2 billion people on both sides. Bilateral trade between China and Arab countries, meanwhile, reached 422 billion U.S. dollars in 2025. According to the foreign affairs office of the Jiangsu provincial government, green energy and digital intelligence have emerged as new growth drivers for cooperation between Jiangsu and Arab countries. In digital intelligence, autonomous driving technologies developed by firms from Jiangsu are making inroads in the Middle East, where they are helping empower local smart mobility and logistics. In infrastructure, a localised optical fibre and cable production base has been set up in Egypt, while large batches of buses have been exported to Algeria, with a knock-down assembly plant built there. ■

item.title: China's railway network handles record 4.13 billion passenger trips in first 10 months of 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
BEIJING, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's railway network handled 4.13 billion passenger trips in the first 10 months of the year, up 4.7 percent year on year and the highest for the period on record, China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. (China Railway) said on Saturday. The rise reflects increased capacity, improved services and stronger support for tourism and international passenger services. During the January-October period, the railway operator ran an average of 11,670 passenger trains per day, up 5 percent year on year, according to the company. Both passenger trips and passenger transport capacity hit single-day records on Oct. 1, the first day of the National Day holiday, with 25.2 million passenger trips recorded and 14,885 trains operated. Beyond regular passenger services, railway authorities have been promoting the integration of rail and tourism. In the first 10 months of 2026, 3,236 dedicated tourism trains were operated, while an additional 1,084 special trains were arranged for concerts, sports events, exhibitions and study tours. These efforts are part of a broader drive to stimulate service consumption and support local economies along rail corridors. Cross-border passenger services also grew strongly in the period. The Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong high-speed railway carried 29.23 million cross-border passengers, up 11 percent year on year, while the China-Laos Railway handled 289,000 cross-border passengers, up 33 percent. China's railways also saw a surge in foreign visitors. A total of 22.52 million foreign passenger trips were made on the national rail network in the first 10 months of 2026, up 32.9 percent year on year, as more international travelers opted to "tour China by train." Official data showed that by the end of 2025, the country's total operating railway mileage had reached 165,000 km, including more than 50,000 km of high-speed rail. China's high-speed rail network is projected to hit 70,000 km by 2035, featuring eight north-south vertical lines and eight east-west horizontal lines. Once complete, the network will connect major cities, city clusters and key economic zones across the country. ■

item.title: China, U.S. hold first meeting of trade council under economic, trade consultation mechanism
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
BEIJING, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- China and the United States held the first meeting of the trade council under the China-U.S. economic and trade consultation mechanism via video link on Friday, China's Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday. Guided by the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, the meeting focused on implementing the outcomes of previous rounds of bilateral economic and trade consultations. The two sides had a candid, in-depth and constructive exchange on tariffs, the reciprocal tariff reduction arrangement covering about 30 billion U.S. dollars worth of each other's goods, agricultural trade and other issues of mutual concern. Both sides will continue to strengthen communication through the trade council, work to resolve their respective economic and trade concerns, further expand cooperation and shorten the list of issues, so as to help build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, the ministry noted. In May 2026, China and the United States agreed to establish a trade council to address their respective concerns in trade cooperation. The two sides held the eighth round of their economic and trade consultations in New York and Washington, D.C. from Sept. 20 to 23. During the consultations, they agreed to reduce tariffs on about 30 billion U.S. dollars worth of goods imported from each other on a reciprocal basis, with tariffs on around 90 percent of the covered products to be lowered to most-favored-nation rates. ■

item.title: Chinese premier calls on Chinese, Thai enterprises to lift bilateral cooperation to higher levels
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
BANGKOK, Nov. 14 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Saturday that Chinese and Thai enterprises should follow the prevailing trend and seize opportunities to elevate their cooperation to higher levels. Li made the remarks while attending a symposium with Chinese and Thai entrepreneurs, along with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, in Bangkok. After listening to remarks from representatives of both countries' business communities, Li said that as China and Thailand work together to usher in a new golden 50 years of bilateral relations, new opportunities are emerging for economic and trade cooperation. To begin with, China and Thailand enjoy the stability brought by high-level mutual trust and friendship, Li said. In today's world marked by turbulence and uncertainty, stability has become a scarce resource, he said, noting that China-Thailand relations and cooperation have demonstrated strong stability. Close and regular communication between the leaders of the two countries, along with strong people-to-people ties and cultural affinity, has provided businesses in both countries with a stable and predictable environment for expanding investment and making long-term plans, Li said. Growing connectivity between the two countries also brings an aggregation effect, Li said. The steady progress in the construction of the China-Thailand railway, the official opening of China's Pinglu Canal, and the strengthening "soft connectivity" in areas such as trade rules, standards and finance have facilitated more seamless interaction of the two markets, enabling more enterprises to generate greater economic benefits, he added. Flourishing innovative cooperation between the two countries also brings an empowering effect, Li said. China-Thailand economic and trade cooperation continues to expand beyond traditional areas into high-tech, emerging and cutting-edge fields, with new business models and areas of growth constantly emerging, he said. This makes it an opportune time for the two sides to leverage their respective strengths and deepen innovation cooperation, Li said. The two sides should upgrade cooperation from "dining tables and taste buds" to "digital intelligence and green development," Li said, calling for expanding traditional trade in agricultural and food products, advancing agricultural modernization in both countries, and pursuing cooperation in emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, clean energy and biomedicine to jointly foster and strengthen new growth drivers. Li called for upgrading cooperation from "production collaboration" to "industrial synergy," adding that the two sides should enhance complementarity and integration in industrial and supply chains, and promote the alignment and mutual recognition of industry standards, to jointly improve competitiveness through more efficient coordination and move up the global value chain. China encourages Chinese enterprises to expand localized operations in Thailand, he added. Li also called for upgrading cooperation from "a bilateral focus" to "regional outreach" by leveraging Thailand's geographic advantages, making good use of policy dividends such as the entry into force of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, and expanding cooperation in third-party markets worldwide to better achieve win-win and multi-win outcomes. The governments of China and Thailand will make active efforts to provide a sound business environment for enterprises of both countries and support their long-term development and deeper engagement in local markets, Li said. He also expressed hope that entrepreneurs from both countries would serve as envoys of friendship among the people and make China-Thailand relations even closer and stronger. For his part, Anutin said China is Thailand's most important trading partner, noting that Thailand hopes to seize the opportunities brought by technological advances and work with China to leverage their respective strengths and achieve higher-quality cooperation. The two countries should move beyond being merely trading partners to becoming long-term partners pursuing common development and mutual success, while further expanding cooperation in electric vehicles, agriculture, investment, connectivity and other areas, Anutin said. Thailand will introduce more policies and measures to create favorable conditions for the long-term operations and development of Chinese enterprises in the country, combat transnational crime and protect the rights and interests of investors, he said. Anutin also expressed confidence that the friendship characterized as "Thailand and China are as close as one family" would yield more tangible results and benefit the peoples of both countries. Speaking at the event, business representatives from both countries briefed the leaders on the progress and outcomes of their cooperation and offered specific suggestions. They expressed full confidence in the China-Thailand friendship and their willingness to further strengthen cooperation and contribute to the development and prosperity of both countries through more practical achievements. ■

item.title: Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, related events in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and deliver remarks, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced Friday. The meeting will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19 under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the spokesperson said. The APEC CEO Summit will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 18 under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the spokesperson said, adding that President Xi will attend the opening ceremony and deliver a keynote speech. President Xi will hold a welcome banquet for participating leaders and representatives, and hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders on the sidelines of the meeting, the spokesperson added. ■
